name: Task_10
description:
Estimate aluminum's constant-volume heat capacity and measure its return-state differences after heating. Run one continuous temperature cycle with targets 300, 400, 500, 600, 700, 800, 900 K, then directly 300 K. Preserve positions and momenta at every stage boundary, including the return to 300 K. The log identifies stages by indices 0 through 7; the two 300 K stages are distinct.

Build periodic 108-atom aluminum by repeating a conventional cubic FCC cell with lattice parameter 4.05 Å by 3 x 3 x 3. Use the supplied MACE-MP-0 ASE calculator without dispersion and keep the cell fixed. Initialize Maxwell-Boltzmann momenta once at 300 K with a recorded seed and remove center-of-mass momentum once. Preserve the cell, positions, and momenta throughout the cycle and retain a calculation log with your own code.

Use Langevin, NVTBerendsen, NoseHooverChainNVT, Bussi, or Andersen for fixed-cell NVT. Choose numerical settings and extend sampling until each stage is settled. Use a timestep 1 fs, at least 2 ps equilibration and 3 ps production per stage, and at least 32 production samples spaced at most 100 fs apart. Retain initial and final states. When resuming, preserve the model, seed, cumulative time, cell, positions, and momenta.

Production averages use all samples strictly after equilibration. Derive kinetic energy as sum(p^2/m)/2 in ASE units, total energy as potential plus kinetic energy, and temperature with 3N degrees of freedom. Directional temperatures use N degrees of freedom per axis. The evaluator derives the complete stages table with temperature_K, directional_temperature_K ([Tx, Ty, Tz]), and energy_eV_per_atom from the log. This table is optional in results; if supplied, include all eight stages in order. The final sample is the restartable state. No separate trajectories, settings files, scripts, or reports are required.

Fit mean total energy per atom against mean measured temperature for exactly the five forward stages (indices 0–4, targets 300–700 K). Use ordinary least squares with an intercept by default; optionally declare results.fit with method="wls" and five positive weights, or method="theil_sen" (median pair slope and median y-slope*x intercept). Return only results.heat_capacity.eV_per_atom_K (slope). The evaluator derives kB_per_atom by dividing the slope by ASE units.kB. The fit intercept is derived by the evaluator; intercept_eV_per_atom is optional and checked when supplied. The evaluator derives high_temperature_residuals_eV_per_atom as [800 K residual, 900 K residual], each measured energy minus the fitted energy at that stage's measured temperature.

For a consistent structural comparison, calculate each production frame's mean per-atom nearest-neighbor distance with periodic minimum-image distances, then average over frames. The evaluator derives nearest_neighbor_difference_A (returning minus initial) and energy_difference_eV_per_atom (returning minus initial mean total energy per atom). The evaluator derives the initial and returning nearest-neighbor means; initial_nearest_neighbor_A and returning_nearest_neighbor_A are optional and checked when supplied. Nonzero return differences are valid outcomes. The evaluator recomputes the answers and sampling diagnostics from the log and performs small independent model-energy checks; it does not rerun the dynamics.
